subject: Re: Privacy Impact Assessment — Redwood usage for PHI pipeline

From: Carolyn Miller <carolyn.miller@healthinsights.com>

Date: 2026-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Privacy Impact Assessment — Redwood usage for PHI pipeline

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is positive about Redwood for inference on our de-identified and pseudonymized PHI. Our legal and privacy team have asked us to complete a DPIA-style template so they can sign off on the processing design before procurement moves forward.

I've attached HealthInsights_DPIA_Template_v1.docx — could you and your security folks fill the sections related to:
- data flows and subprocessors
- transfers outside the EU (we rely on SCCs)
- retention and deletion guarantees for inference outputs
- risk mitigations for profiling and sensitive attribute inference

Quick context: the workload will include pseudonymized clinical notes and device telemetry (no raw images). Retention requirement from our side is 7 years post-treatment for analytics. We also need evidence artifacts: a simple data flow diagram, SOC 2 evidence reference, and any DPA/DDA text you use for downstream subprocessors.

Timing: procurement is aiming for a DPIA packet by Apr 20. Is that feasible? If not, please propose next steps and an expected delivery window.

Thanks — feel free to loop in whoever on your side needs to own the evidence pack.

Carolyn
Carolyn Miller
Privacy Program Manager, HealthInsights

Hi Carolyn — thanks for sending this and for the clear scope. We're happy to support and can get a completed DPIA packet to you. Proposed next steps: 

1) We will prepare a filled copy of your template with narrative answers and attach: a) a concise data flow diagram b) SOC 2 references (report hash + control descriptions) c) draft DPA/processing addendum language for subprocessors.
2) I will own coordination and deliver the initial draft by Thu Apr 16. Marissa (security & compliance) will review the technical/evidence artifacts. Dylan (solutions) will confirm the exact telemetry fields we expect to see so the data-classification language matches your template.

A couple of clarifying questions that will speed things up:
- Can you confirm whether the clinical notes will include free-text PHI (names/IDs) that you will pseudonymize before sending, or do you expect Redwood to receive tokenized identifiers?
- Do you require us to demonstrate SCCs explicitly in the DPIA (we can reference standard SCC text and our DPA) or do you need a signed Appendix of SCCs attached?

If the Apr 16 draft works we should have time for your legal to review before the Apr 20 procurement deadline. If you prefer, we can also run a short evidence review call — suggested slots attached.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachments: proposed-evidence-review-slots.ics (text/calendar)

Thanks Aditya — answers below inline and attaching a quick data flow image so you and Marissa have the exact pipeline we expect.

- Clinical notes: we will pseudonymize at source; notes will still contain rich clinical context and free-text clinical observations (no direct identifiers).
- SCCs: procurement would like explicit confirmation that SCCs are used for EU->US transfer and to see the clause text in the DPIA packet. A signed Appendix is not strictly required at this stage but will be needed before any cross-border processing goes live.
- Retention: 7 years post-treatment in our systems; for outputs returned by Redwood we need a clear retention/deletion SLA and an option to scrub cached prefixes on demand.

Attached: HealthInsights_DataFlow.png (image/png) — shows pseudonymization step, batch inference in Redwood, and results returned to HealthInsights.

Procurement note: they will want references to SOC 2 Type II report and a named list of subprocessors (and whether any subprocessors access cleartext outputs).

Let us know if Apr 16 is still good. If so, please send the draft packet and we will prioritize legal review.

Carolyn

Carolyn — attaching our completed DPIA packet and the evidence artifacts for your legal review. Summary of what we delivered: 

Attachments (see attached files in this thread):
- Redwood_DPIA_Response_HealthInsights_20260415.docx — filled template with narrative answers, risk assessment, and mitigation map.
- HealthInsights_DataFlow.png — annotated copy showing processing stages and where pseudonymization occurs.
- DataProcessing_Addendum.pdf — draft DPA + SCC reference text we use for EU->US transfers.

Key points / short answers:
- Data flows: Redwood receives pseudonymized clinical text + telemetry. No downstream subprocessors receive cleartext inference outputs unless explicitly enabled by the customer; our default config keeps outputs encrypted in transit and at rest with customer keying options.
- SCCs & transfers: the attached DPA contains SCC clause text we reference; we can produce a signed Appendix when procurement is ready.
- Retention: default inference result retention is 24 hours; configurable retention windows (including immediate purge) are available in Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted API, we provide purge-on-request and encrypted-at-rest guarantees documented in the packet.
- SOC 2 evidence: we included the SOC 2 report hash and a pointer to the secure drive with the full report.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the draft answers map correctly to your template sections and whether legal needs additional artifacts (e.g., architecture diagrams, copy of KMS policy).
2) If procurement proceeds, we can bring in our legal team to finalize the DPA and SCC Appendix; Marissa can assist with any technical control clarifications.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min call this week with Marissa to walk through the packet.

Best,
